html:
The Kingdom of Norway is the realm formed when the petty kingdoms of the Norwegian coast were joined under one king. On the map for 900 it is the young kingdom of the Viking Age.

Tradition says Harald Fairhair won the battle of Hafrsfjord around 872 and became the first king of all Norway, though his real power was mainly in the west, and the date may be later. Sagas say chieftains who would not accept him sailed off in the settlement of Iceland.

After him the kingdom often split again. Christian kings, Olaf Tryggvason and then Olaf II, forced conversion around 1000; Olaf's death at Stiklestad in 1030 made him Norway's patron saint. Norway later joined Denmark in Denmark-Norway and Sweden in Sweden-Norway before full independence in 1905. See Northmen for the land before the kingdom and Norway for later centuries.
